body:
## What happened

Base: `dev@56575e062`, 2026-09-14. Configuration is the shipped default —
`routing = "simple"`, `lane.talk = "auto"`.

Over 1.71 days of ordinary use (`~/.aforge/logs/calls.jsonl`,
2026-09-12T11:53 → 2026-09-14T04:50, 4,828 priced calls, 90.5M prompt tokens),
**40.3% of consecutive calls inside one conversation were served by a different
machine than the call before them**, and a call that changed machine missed the
prompt cache outright **4.7× more often** than one that did not:

```
previous call SAME endpoint : 36 full misses of 423 calls = 8.5%
previous call OTHER endpoint: 70 full misses of 176 calls = 39.8%

first-call-of-stream misses (unavoidable):  22, $0.24
MID-STREAM full misses (avoidable in principle): 262, $10.15
   of which the served endpoint CHANGED from the previous call: 201, $9.23
```

Worked example rows (model, previous endpoint → this endpoint, previous
prompt/cached, this prompt, this cost):

```
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash  Io Net   -> Venice   102062/0      102935  $0.0394
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash  Venice   -> Parasail 105092/16384  106095  $0.0321
deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash  Parasail -> Wafer     48287/0       51261  $0.0157
z-ai/glm-5.3                  Friendli -> DigitalOcean 47587/42688 56233 $0.0546
```

The worst single stream was `moonshotai/kimi-k3` — 139 calls, 17.2M prompt
tokens, $16.18, **46 endpoint hops across 11 distinct machines**.

$9.23 over 1.71 days is **≈$5.40/day**, against $54.44 of recorded spend in the
same window: roughly one dollar in six.

This is exactly the failure `internal/provider/affinity.go` was written to close,
and `internal/provider/velocity.go`'s own comment states the stake in the same
figure the data reproduces:

> it names the one machine that already holds this lineage's prompt prefix, and a
> cold prefix cost 4.7× a warm one at identical token counts

The pin never reaches the wire on the shipped default. `providerPreferences`
returns before the line that reads the pin.

## Replication

**Deterministic (no model).**

Run the law that blesses it — it passes today, and its own assertion is the
defect:

```
go test ./internal/provider/ -run TestSimpleModeSendsOnlyThePersonsPin -v
```

`internal/provider/simplemode_verify_test.go` asserts that an unpinned request
under `simple` carries `Order == nil`. It does, because in
`providerPreferences` (search `SIMPLE ROUTING SENDS THE PERSON'S OWN
INSTRUCTION`) the `RoutingSimple` branch returns before `heldEndpoint` — the
only read of the affinity ledger onto the wire — is ever reached. With a lane
row in force the same branch calls `applyLaneChoice` with an empty `pinned`
argument, so the pin is dropped on that road too.

The second half of the reproduction is that **no test exercises the shipped
default at all**: `internal/provider/affinity_test.go` has 14 tests and 12
occurrences of `StaticRouting(RoutingLatency)` and **zero** of `RoutingSimple`.
Take any of them — `TestTheSecondRequestAsksForTheEndpointThatServedTheFirst` is
the clearest — change `StaticRouting(RoutingLatency)` to
`StaticRouting(RoutingSimple)` and it fails: the second request carries no
`order` at all. `config.DefaultRouting` is `RoutingSimple` and has been since
the build that moved it off `latency` (search `IT WAS \`latency\` UNTIL THIS
BUILD` in `internal/config/settings.go`).

**Field (real models).**

Needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, about twenty minutes and a few cents. Drive a real
conversation of ten or more turns with a long prefix (attach a folder, or let it
read a few files) on a model served by many machines —
`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` has seventeen — then read the call log the build
always writes:

```sh
AFORGE_HOME=/tmp/pinrepro bin/aforge chat            # ten turns, tools allowed
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, collections
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open('/tmp/pinrepro/logs/calls.jsonl')]
rows = [r for r in rows if r.get('phase') != 'start'
        and r.get('tag') in ('turn', 'task', 'leaf')
        and r.get('prompt_tokens', 0) >= 2000]
rows.sort(key=lambda r: r['ts'])
g = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows:
    g[(r.get('run'), r.get('node'), r.get('model'))].append(r)
same = [0, 0]; diff = [0, 0]
for v in g.values():
    for i in range(1, len(v)):
        hop = v[i]['served'] != v[i-1]['served']
        (diff if hop else same)[1] += 1
        if v[i].get('cached_tokens', 0) == 0:
            (diff if hop else same)[0] += 1
print('same endpoint :', same, 'other endpoint:', diff)
PY
```

Today the `other endpoint` bucket exists at all, and its miss rate is several
times the `same endpoint` bucket's. The control run is the same conversation
with `routing` set to `latency` in `~/.aforge/config.json` — the previous
default, where `heldEndpoint` is reached and the pin rides in `provider.order`.

A six-turn conversation is **not** enough to see it: in three six-turn control
runs on the Spark the router happened to hold one machine for all six turns and
the hit rate was 97–99% throughout. The hopping shows up on long conversations
with large prefixes.

## Where

- `internal/provider/velocity.go` — `providerPreferences`, the branch marked
  `SIMPLE ROUTING SENDS THE PERSON'S OWN INSTRUCTION AND NOTHING ELSE`, and
  `heldEndpoint` below it.
- `internal/provider/lanes.go` — `applyLaneChoice`, and the `ownLane` guard that
  strips the cache pin when a person's lane row is in force.
- `internal/provider/affinity.go` — `noteEndpointAffinity`, which gates only on
  `RoutingOff`, so the ledger is written on every answer under `simple` and read
  by nothing.
- `internal/lane/choose.go` — `cachedTokens`, the cache-aware half of the lane
  chooser, unreachable on the same road.
- `internal/provider/simplemode_verify_test.go` —
  `TestSimpleModeSendsOnlyThePersonsPin`, the law that currently blesses it.
- `internal/config/settings.go` — `DefaultRouting`.

## The fix

**A cache pin is not a routing preference. It is the address of this
conversation's own prefix, and `simple` should send it.**

`simple` promises that what a person asked for is what goes on the wire — no
sort word, no price ceiling, no speed ranking of ours. The warm-endpoint pin is
none of those: it does not rank machines by anything this process believes about
them, it names the one machine that is already holding bytes this conversation
has paid for. Leaving it off does not make the request more faithful to what the
person asked for; it makes the same request cost 4.7× more.

So under `simple`, with no lane row in force, the body carries
`{"order": ["<held>"], "allow_fallbacks": true}` and nothing else — a preference
and never a demand, exactly as it rides under `latency` today, so a busy or
absent machine still just does not answer and the router picks as before. With a
person's lane row in force the pin stays out: the row is the person naming a
machine, and that has always won.

`TestSimpleModeSendsOnlyThePersonsPin`'s wording changes with it: an unpinned
`simple` request is bare **except for the endpoint that holds its prefix**.

## Acceptance

- **e2e:** `go test -tags e2e ./internal/provider/ -run TestRealRouter -v`
  against a model with a dozen machines: a conversation of eight requests under
  the shipped default reports the same `served` endpoint on at least seven of
  them, and the second request's body carries `provider.order[0] == ` the
  endpoint that served the first. Exit 0.
- **e2e:** the control — the same eight requests with a `lane.talk` row set to a
  named machine send `{"only": [name], "allow_fallbacks": false}` and **no**
  `order`, i.e. a person's pin still wins outright and nothing else is asked for.
- **Unit:** every test in `internal/provider/affinity_test.go` runs under
  `config.DefaultRouting` rather than a hardcoded mode, and a structural law
  fails the build if an affinity test names a routing strategy literal — the
  default moved out from under this whole mechanism with every gate green, and
  that is the thing to make impossible rather than to fix once.
- The manual page that covers routing and the `lane` row quotes the new wording
  (`internal/manual/chat/`), and the change entry's `invalidates` says that under
  `simple` a request used to carry no endpoint preference at all, so a
  conversation's prefix went cold every time the router moved it.

comments.body:
Per-call-kind breakdown of the same log window, same grouping ((run, node, model) in time order), both calls in a transition carrying ≥2000 prompt tokens:

```
tag     transitions   hop%    miss | same endpoint     miss | hopped
turn        328       23.5%     23/251 =  9.2%          32/77  = 41.6%
task        110       80.0%      0/22  =  0.0%          32/88  = 36.4%
leaf        197       10.7%     13/176 =  7.4%          13/21  = 61.9%
```

The task road is the worst of the three: **80% of consecutive task calls change machine**, and every full cache miss on that road is on a call that had just hopped — none at all on the 22 transitions that stayed. It matches the aggregate hit rates over the same window:

```
tag     calls   prompt tokens   cached tokens   hit%       $
turn     2061      52,263,959      40,825,510   78.1   22.78
task     1396      28,125,428      13,183,855   46.9    5.22
leaf      535       8,760,307       7,440,268   84.9    0.79
```

`task` sits at 46.9% against `turn`'s 78.1% and `leaf`'s 84.9%, on 28M prompt tokens. Whatever the fix does for the conversation, the task road needs it more.

Second, stricter estimate of the money, using a five-minute warm window instead of just the immediately preceding call.

For every call with ≥2000 prompt tokens, `expected` = the largest prompt any call in the same (run, node, model) lineage sent in the previous five minutes (capped at this call's own prompt — i.e. what a warm neighbour could have served); `unwarmed` = `expected − cached_tokens`, priced at `prompt_price − cache_read_price` from the model catalog. Same log window (2026-09-12T11:53 → 2026-09-14T04:50, 1.71 days).

```
previous call on the SAME machine : 643 calls,  3,362,771 unwarmed tokens,  $1.25  (mean $0.0020/call)
previous call on ANOTHER machine  : 828 calls, 20,335,213 unwarmed tokens, $11.02  (mean $0.0133/call)
```

Holding the hopped calls to the same-machine mean:

```
excess attributable to hopping: $9.40 over 1.71 days = $5.50/day
every unwarmed prefix byte:    $12.27 over 1.71 days = $7.18/day
```

$5.50/day against $31.80/day of recorded spend in the same window — about one dollar in six, and it agrees with the independent full-miss estimate in the issue body ($5.40/day) to within two per cent.

One more fact worth having on the issue: **the pin ledger is process-local in-memory with no expiry** (`sharedPins` in `internal/provider/affinity.go`, and the type comment says so). So even under `latency` a pin exists only inside one long-lived process — `aforge chat --once`, `aforge do` and every headless door start cold every time. Verified on the wire: six `--once` turns under `routing: latency` all sent `{"sort":"latency", "allow_fallbacks":true, "require_parameters":true, "max_price":{…}}` and **no `order`** on any of them. That is correct for a memory ledger and is not the defect here, but it means a fix that only reaches the interactive surface leaves the headless doors where they are.

Field drive on the Spark, the real `bin/aforge chat` in tmux under the shipped default (`routing: simple`, `lane.talk: auto`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), one long-lived process, seven turns about three minutes apart. Every turn was served by the same endpoint and the prefix was byte-stable, and the cache still went cold five times out of eight:

```
04:52:08  prompt 14037  cached  1536  hit 10.9%  $0.001146
04:55:01  prompt 14201  cached  9728  hit 68.5%  $0.000580
04:57:59  prompt 14279  cached 14080  hit 98.6%  $0.000276
05:00:44  prompt 14341  cached     0  hit  0.0%  $0.001277
05:03:35  prompt 14183  cached     0  hit  0.0%  $0.001269
05:06:28  prompt 14468  cached  1536  hit 10.6%  $0.001182
05:09:22  prompt 14530  cached     0  hit  0.0%  $0.001304
```

Cold $0.00127 against warm $0.00028 — 4.6×, the same ratio again. That decay is the remote cache's own lifetime and not this build's doing, **but it is the reason the pin matters more than the hop rate alone suggests**: `internal/lane` already believes something about which endpoint is still holding a prefix (`PrefixHold = 5 * time.Minute`, `internal/lane/value.go`; priced in `cachedTokens` in `internal/lane/choose.go`), and under `simple` the chooser that would use that belief is only consulted when a lane is pinned. So the default turns off both halves at once: the pin that says *go back to the machine that holds your bytes*, and the belief that says *which machines still hold them*.

For contrast, the same six turns sent seconds apart rather than minutes apart hit 97–99% on every turn after the first. The 78.1% aggregate in the field log is the mixture of the two.

title: the warm-endpoint cache pin never reaches the wire under the shipped `simple` routing, and 40% of a conversation's calls hop machine — $5.40/day of cold prefixes
